nodes.summary: For every type $A$, the map sending an element of the inversion twist of $A$ to its underlying element of $A$ is a bijection, whose inverse sends $a \in A$ to its copy in the twist.
nodes.title: Underlying bijection of the inversion twist

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $\iota$ the inversion of the group ring $R[G]$. For every $x \in R[G]$, $\iota(\iota(x)) = x$.
nodes.title: Group-ring inversion is an involution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $G$ a commutative group. For every $g \in G$ and $r \in R$, the inversion of the group ring $R[G]$ sends $r\, g$ to $r\, g^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Inversion on basis elements

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a module over the group ring $R[G]$. The inversion twist of $A$ is a copy of $A$ with the same addition, on which $r \in R[G]$ acts by $a \mapsto \iota(r) \cdot a$, where $\iota$ is the inversion of $R[G]$ and $\cdot$ is the original action on $A$.
nodes.title: Inversion twist of a group-ring module

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $G$ a commutative group. The inversion of the group ring $R[G]$ is the ring automorphism of $R[G]$ induced by the group automorphism $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ of $G$: it sends $\sum_g r_g\, g$ to $\sum_g r_g\, g^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Inversion on a group ring

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a module over the group ring $R[G]$. The map sending an element of the inversion twist of the inversion twist of $A$ to its underlying element of $A$ is an $R[G]$-linear isomorphism.
nodes.title: Twisting twice by inversion recovers the module

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a module over the group ring $R[G]$. For every $r \in R[G]$ and every element $a$ of the inversion twist of $A$, with underlying element $\bar a \in A$, the underlying element of $r \cdot a$ is $\iota(r) \cdot \bar a$, where $\iota$ is the inversion of $R[G]$ and $\cdot$ on the right is the original action on $A$.
nodes.title: Scalar action on the inversion twist

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
